title: Balrampur Chini Mills Ltd - 500038 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Balrampur Chini FY26 sugar cane crush rose 5.2% to 1,043 lakh quintals despite cane price hike to INR400/quintal; ethanol price revision still pending.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a stable year: cane crushed rose 5.2% to 1,043 lakh quintals, gross recovery eased to 11.24% from 11.28%, and higher volumes and stable realisations offset a INR30/quintal rise in cane price (INR370 to INR400). Distillery volumes rose but margins stayed under pressure because ethanol prices have not been revised for three years. The PLA (polylactic acid) plant is nearing commissioning, with capex now INR3,080 crore and a INR450 crore preferential issue approved, promoters taking INR193 crore. Management said the government export ban followed lower yields in Maharashtra, UP and Karnataka, and that the sugar stock outlook is supportive.

financial_highlights.change: no dilution per management; promoters subscribing INR193 crore

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: FY26 cane crush up 5.2% to 1,043 lakh quintals; recovery 11.24%. Management says 0238 variety replacement is tough, but new varieties show promise and it looks like the bottom.

segments.name: Distillery / Ethanol
segments.commentary: FY26 output about 27 crore litres; margins under pressure as B-heavy and juice-route prices unrevised for three years. Mix shifted towards B-heavy/juice route, with C-heavy reduced.

segments.name: PLA (polylactic acid)
segments.commentary: Plant about six months into operations; imports and market seeding underway with Sulzer as technology supplier. Revenue so far small; no offtake disclosed. Targets 35% EBITDA margin, excluding incentives.

segments.name: Auxilo Financial Services
segments.commentary: Mentioned in the presentation, but no impact details were given on the call; management referred analysts to the uploaded financials.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to 35% EBITDA margin for PLA; incentives (capital subsidy and interest subvention) excluded from this target as they sit below EBITDA.
Govt ethanol price revision for juice/B-heavy routes seen as likely; management says 'I think it will get done' but is cautious given past delays.
Industry sugar closing stock projected at about 4.3 million tonnes after 0.7 million tonnes of exports; management calls the balance supportive for prices.
Next PLA capacity expansion could take about 15 months, with commissioning of the current expansion expected in Q3 of this year (per Q&A, timeline 'October').
capex_capacity: PLA project capex revised to INR3,080 crore; integrated value chain expansion including a lacto-gypsum processing plant at Kumbhi to make gypsum board from PLA by-product gypsum.
Ethanol nameplate capacity can reach 34-35 crore litres against FY26 output of about 27 crore litres; juice and B-heavy routes needed to fill capacity.
PLA first-phase project took about 2 years 9 months; management said a next expansion could take about 15 months.
Capex commissioning targeted for Q3 of this year (Q&A).
demand_pricing: UP sugar prices in Rs 41-42 per kg range; management expects steady to gradually firmer prices given low closing stock of about 4.3 million tonnes.
Export of about 0.7 million tonnes went out before government prohibited further exports after production moderation.
Management says fossil plastic prices have risen sharply with crude, lifting PLA prices; customers want committed volumes and delivery schedules before replacing existing suppliers.
Gutka and non-plastic mandates: central government mandate, UP government committee and direct customers form a three-pronged approach. Timeline for detailed mandate not given.

qa_highlights.question: What shelf life and barrier packaging validation has been done for gutka use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said barrier properties, duration, and food-safety contact testing were completed without issues.

qa_highlights.question: Could there be a timeline for government mandates on non-plastic and PLA use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management referenced central and UP government mandates (UP committee formed) and customer demand; said 'so far, so good' but gave no date. Chairman said it is not expected within 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will PLA margins reach 35% and does this include incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the 35% EBITDA target excludes incentives, which are capital subsidy and interest subvention and sit below EBITDA. Sugarcane and bagasse proximity, plus lower logistics and energy costs, support the margin view.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ethanol output shifted toward B-heavy and juice routes when C-heavy prices were revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix was optimised after expecting a price revision that did not come. Juice and B-heavy are needed to use capacity, and tenders were filed in November; approach will be more cautious this year.

qa_highlights.question: Any progress on ethanol price revision and sugar cane impact from fertiliser availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said talks on quantum and price are serious, and crude at Rs 111 and currency at Rs 96 support the case. On crop, yield impact cannot be assessed before September-October; mid-August rainfall is the key checkpoint.

qa_highlights.question: How do PLA and ethanol volumes and E85/E100 demand look?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: FY26 ethanol output was 27 crore litres with capacity of 34-35 crore litres; price drives the juice versus C-heavy mix. Automakers have prototypes and the government has a draft notification for E85 and E100.

risks_watch: Ethanol price revision still pending; margins in distillery remain under pressure until the government acts.
PLA offtake and customer qualification not yet disclosed; existing customers are waiting for production to start before switching suppliers.
PLA revenue remains small; ramp-up and commercial volumes are yet to be seen.
Crop yield and rainfall in August-September may influence the FY27 cane outlook; fertiliser availability also flagged.
Mandate timing (central, UP, and customers) for non-plastic and biodegradable products remains uncertain.
Ethanol capacity over-supply at the industry level; government moves on E20+ blending pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on PLA margins, demand and sugar pricing, but evasive on specific offtake agreements, customer names and Auxilo impact. Management is cautious on ethanol pricing timing, saying 'once bitten, twice shy'.
key_quotes: And just to let everyone know, UP crushed 7% lower cane than last year and we have crushed 5.2% higher cane.
Giving more details is not proper right now. Because everything is nearing finalization, and to give you, you know, let it get finalized.
We have not considered the benefit of incentive while guiding 35% EBITDA margin.
So, definitely positive conversation has begun, especially crude at Rs. 111, currency at Rs. 96, we know the cost.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; FY26 cane crush rose 5.2% to 1,043 lakh quintals, while PLA plant (INR3,080 crore capex, commissioning Q3 CY2026) and a likely ethanol price revision are the main growth levers, with ethanol nameplate of 34-35 crore litres versus ~27 crore litres output in FY26 but no firm volume plan.
